cont_mlp.why_the_dash: this family has no refusal verb: asked for a deleted value or a deleted conjunction it emits a feature vector like any other request. footnote: MLP / mlp_180k / continuous-input MLP / transformer / LSTM take a DASH on row 7's refusal half: measured here, every one of them refuses 0.0000 of the deleted requests, because none of them has a refusal verb at all. LACE and PoE-EBM take a dash for a different reason -- spoke A's own API declines to expose them as request->features callables, because their output is a sampler draw rather than a function of the request -- and both sit far outside the byte pin (95.1x and 27.1x). POPULATION: every shipped rival here is fitted on the Montero combination pool and is NOT like-for-like with a value-holdout arm on a whole-value row, so these read-backs are descriptive and are NOT placed beside the field store as a contest. A dash is never a win for us.

not_callable.lace: 'lace': LACE's output is a SAMPLER DRAW, not a function of the request alone: two calls on the same request return different features by construction. It is therefore not offered as a request->features callable. Its categorical head also has a closed vocabulary over the realised grid, so it cannot express an off-grid value at all - a structural limit of the method, documented at chlu.core.gen_request.DenseRequests, not one this spoke imposed. Hubs needing LACE on their own corners should ask this spoke to score those corners.
not_callable.poe_ebm: 'poe_ebm': The product-of-experts EBM's output is an SGLD draw from a noise initialisation, not a function of the request alone, and its experts are conditioned on a FULL factor assignment. It is not offered as a request->features callable. Hubs needing it on their own corners should ask this spoke to score those corners.
